title: Mark a helicopter landing zone: corner beacons 100 ft or more apart, the fifth upwind
instruction: A medical helicopter is coming to land on this field (1:110 scale). Mark its landing zone on the grass: an orange beacon at each corner of a zone at least 100 by 100 ft (277 mm) with square corners. Then stand the blue beacon just outside the middle of the zone's upwind side, 1 to 6 m (10 to 55 mm) beyond it. The windsock streams downwind. Every beacon must stand upright on the grass on its own.
context: Firefighters and EMTs (O*NET 33-2011.00, 29-2042.00) set up landing zones for air-medical helicopters at road crashes and rural scenes. Services commonly ask for a zone of about 100 x 100 ft (30 x 30 m) on firm, level, open ground, a beacon, cone or light at each corner and a fifth marker on the upwind side, so the pilot can read the wind and land into it; the crew reads the wind from a windsock, smoke or flags. Nothing is marked out here: the zone has to be sized against a minimum, squared, kept on the grass with room left for the wind marker, and the marker put on the side the sock says the wind comes from. At 1:110 the field is 37 x 40 m and 100 ft is 277 mm; the beacons are over-scale so they can be gripped. Two orange beacons and the blue wait on the road at the left, two orange on the parking strip at the right, so each arm fetches its own side's: gripping from above, neither arm reaches the other side's beacons.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A helicopter landing site at 1:110; seven kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Grass field: a green artificial-turf mat 1 mm thick fixed to the table, x 13.0 to 46.5 cm, y -17.0 to +19.0 cm (335 x 360 mm, 37 x 40 m at scale). (2) Road: a dark grey vinyl sheet 1 mm thick fixed along the field's left edge, x 10.0 to 48.0 cm, y +19.0 to +26.0 cm. (3) Parking strip: a light grey vinyl sheet 1 mm thick fixed along the field's right edge, x 10.0 to 48.0 cm, y -25.0 to -17.0 cm. The three mats' tops are flush. (4) Fire engine: a red-painted wooden block 90 mm long (along x), 24 mm wide and 27 mm tall, fixed on the parking strip, x 28.5 to 37.5 cm, y -20.8 to -18.4 cm. (5) Windsock: a white-painted wooden mast 10 mm across and 90 mm tall fixed upright on the table at x 45.0 cm, y +33.0 cm, beyond the road; at its top a sleeve of stiffened fabric in five 12 mm long bands, orange, white, orange, white and orange, square in section and tapering from 18 to 16, 14, 12 and 10 mm, runs from the mast toward the field (y +32.5 to +26.5 cm, its axis 80 mm above the table, 71 to 89 mm up at the mouth). The sleeve streams toward -y: the wind blows from +y (the left, over the road) toward -y. Nothing moves it. (6) Four orange beacons: loose orange plastic cylinders 28 mm across and 28 mm tall, 40 g each (a weighted base), both ends alike, standing upright: two on the road centred at x 20.0 and 26.0 cm, y +22.5 cm, and two on the parking strip centred at x 20.0 and 24.0 cm, y -21.5 cm. (7) Blue beacon: the same in blue, standing on the road centred at x 32.0 cm, y +22.5 cm. Nothing else is on the table. The beacons stand for road LED beacons and are over-scale (28 mm is about 3 m at 1:110) so a gripper can hold them; distances are read between their centres.
scoring: End state: the score is read from the five beacons at the last step, as a tape between beacon centres and a protractor on a top photo would read it once the arms have withdrawn; the simulator also gives each gripper's pad-tip point (midway between its finger tips) and how far it is open. A beacon's tilt is the angle of its axis from vertical (either end up). A beacon is 'placed' when it is tilted at most 10 degrees, its lowest point is within 3 mm of the grass top (not on another beacon or held up), its centre, seen from above, is inside the grass outline (x 13.0 to 46.5 cm, y -17.0 to +19.0 cm), and it is let go: no gripper's pad-tip point is less than 10 mm above its top while within that gripper's finger reach of its axis (79 mm fully open, 50 mm closed on a beacon, over every yaw: a finger touching or propping it holds it). Score 0 if any orange beacon is not placed (left on the road or the strip, tipped, stacked, off the grass, still held). Otherwise join the four orange centres in order of angle round their centroid into the zone: four sides, centre to centre, and four corners. Square: 0.5 if every side is at least 277 mm (100 ft) and every corner 80 to 100 degrees; 0.25 if every side is at least 249 mm (90 ft) and every corner 70 to 110 degrees; otherwise the score is 0. Wind marker: the upwind side is the zone's side whose outward direction (square to it, away from the zone) is nearest to +y, where the wind comes from (if two tie, either counts). Let d be the blue centre's distance outside that side's line and t its position along the side (0 at one corner, 1 at the other). 0.5 if the blue beacon is placed, d is 10 to 55 mm (1 to 6 m) and t is 1/3 to 2/3 (the middle third); 0.25 if it is placed, d is over 0 and at most 100 mm and t is 0 to 1, but not all of the 0.5 conditions hold; otherwise 0 (inside the zone, beside another side, past a corner, more than 100 mm out, not placed). Score = square + wind marker. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Every outcome: a 292 mm zone square to the field with the blue 30 mm outside the middle of its left (upwind) side: 1.0; the same with the blue beside a corner of that side (t under 1/3) or 5 mm out: 0.75; a 280 mm zone with the blue 70 mm out: 0.75; a 260 mm zone with the blue 30 mm out mid upwind side: 0.75; a 292 mm zone with the blue outside its right (downwind) side (the sock misread), inside it, or still gripped on its spot: 0.5; a 260 mm zone with the blue beside a corner of the upwind side: 0.5; a 260 mm zone with the blue downwind: 0.25; a 166 mm (60 ft) zone, a 250 mm zone with 65 degree corners, an orange beacon used as the wind marker (the blue at a corner), an orange beacon left on the road or still gripped at its corner: 0. The blue must stand on the grass too, so the upwind side must be at least 10 mm inside the field's left edge (y +18.0 cm at most): the zone needs room for its marker. Any orange beacon may be any corner. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held with every beacon still (its centre moving under 5 mm in all over the last 0.5 s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction. The mats, fire engine and windsock are fixed; no wind is simulated, so the sleeve is a stiff fixed shape that shows the wind. The field, zone and distances are at 1:110; the beacons and the windsock are over-scale so they can be gripped and seen, and the beacons are upright cylinders where real LED beacons are flat pucks. The grippers are read only to check that each beacon was let go.
reset_notes: Stand the orange beacons back upright on the road centred at x 20.0 and 26.0 cm, y +22.5 cm, and on the parking strip centred at x 20.0 and 24.0 cm, y -21.5 cm, and the blue beacon on the road centred at x 32.0 cm, y +22.5 cm. The mats, fire engine and windsock are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
